28988.etyen:
Derived from Ancient Greek κᾰτᾰστροφή (kătăstrophḗ, “overturning; subjugation; end, conclusion; ruin”), from Ancient Greek κᾰτᾰστρέφω (kătăstréphō, “to turn down, bring down, subdue”) + -η (-ē, “noun-forming suffix”). κᾰτᾰστρέφω (kătăstréphō) is formed from κᾰτᾰ- (kătă-, “back; downwards; against; completely”) + στρέφω (stréphō, “to turn, twist”).
κᾰτᾰ- (kătă-) is the prefixal form of κατά (katá, “down; against; according to”), from Proto-Hellenic *kətá, perhaps from Proto-Indo-European *ḱm̥-th₂, itself from Proto-Indo-European *ḱóm (“beside, with”).
The deeper origin of στρέφω (stréphō) is di

1004860.etyen:
From the definite article de (“the”) + små (“small”) + Antiller (“the Antilles”), literally “the small Antilles”.
Synchronically, små (“small”) is the plural and definite form corresponding to liten (“small”). It is inherited from Old Norse smár (“small”), from Proto-Germanic *smalaz (“small, narrow”). Cognates include Norwegian Nynorsk små, Danish små, Swedish små, Icelandic smár, English small and German schmal (“narrow”).
The final element is the form Antiller, used in standardized fixed geographical names beginning with an article and adjective; the standalone geographical name is Antillen

1005116.etyen:
From giss (“G-sharp”) + -iss (“sharp; raised by a semitone”), effectively applying -iss (“sharp”) a second time. The suffix -iss is from German German -is (“sharp”); its further origin is uncertain.
